description: Power Grid Model is a library for steady-state analysis of electricity distribution networks, with a C++ core and Python and C interfaces. It computes power flow, state estimation and short-circuit calculations. It is developed as an LF Energy project by contributors including staff of the Dutch distribution operator Alliander, as listed in its citation file. The method is location-independent. It is installed from PyPI or conda-forge, with documentation on Read the Docs, example notebooks in a workshop repository, and companion packages for converting other grid formats (power-grid-model-io) and a data science interface (power-grid-model-ds). Version 1.13.176 was released on 25 September 2026 and every release is archived on Zenodo. It is licensed under MPL-2.0 at no cost. Caveats: the scope is steady-state calculation only, with no dynamics or optimisation, and the current package needs Python 3.12 or later. Simulation uses are network flow studies, operational digital twins of distribution grids and hosting capacity and planning assessments. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
